sentence: This project develops a laser process that prints tiny objects layer by layer from nanoparticles and studies how the printed materials change.
This project builds an optical imaging method to watch how lithium moves through battery materials while they are working.
This project studies how large earthquakes rupture around the world, using waves recorded by seismic arrays to measure how fast and how far they travel.
This project uses a microscope to identify and measure microplastic particles in water, soils, and biological tissues.
This project designs and builds very thin memory devices called memristors, made from oxide films, for computing inspired by how brains work.
This project links research networks from several countries so scientists can work together on studying the near-surface environment of the Earth.
This project builds machine learning methods that use single-cell data to track the cell cycle and how cells change as they develop.
This project studies how a roundworm trades off surviving starvation against growing quickly after food returns, and which molecular processes cause it.
This project builds deep learning methods that use seismic waves to estimate the structure underground and the sources of earthquakes together.
This project studies shapes described by polynomial equations, including their singularities, using ideas from several areas of mathematics.
This project builds mathematical and artificial intelligence tools to predict how disease, pesticides, and other threats together harm honeybee colonies.
This project builds a small testing device that uses a vibrating tip to make tiny droplets and detect nucleic acids and proteins in a sample.
This project builds deep learning models that read brain signals to decode speech and to find brain regions that matter for language.
This project holds a workshop where researchers discuss how to make AI foundation models trustworthy in networked systems.
This project studies AI tools that estimate a person's risk of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure from routine scans and health records.
This project builds a system that monitors airborne pathogens in real time and studies how to tell communities about the risks.
This project studies how people see the 3D shape of objects from patterns of light and shading.
This project studies how virus infections without symptoms affect the flight and health of honey bees, and how heat stress and antiviral defenses matter.
